newsitem.title: USA: CIGNA to use most proceeds for repurchase.
newsitem.headline: CIGNA to use most proceeds for repurchase.

text.p: CIGNA Corp said it expects to use a "signficant amount" of the proceeds from the sale of its individual life insurance and annuity business for share repurchase.
CIGNA agreed to sell its individual life and annuity business to Lincoln National Corp for $1.4 billion cash.
CIGNA spokesman Michael Monroe valued the deal at $1.6 billion, noting that the company will retain the statutory surplus from the business, which at the end of 1996 was about $225 million.
Internal growth and acquisitions, as well as share repurchase, are high priorities for CIGNA, Monroe said.
But, he said, the company does not have much appetite for another large acquisition at the moment, following its recent $1.7 billion acquisition of Healthsource Inc.
In the near-term, he said, the logical alternative use for the proceeds will be share repurchase.
"A significant amount of these proceeds will be used for share repurchase," Monroe said.
Asked how much of the proceeds will be used for repurchase, he said: "I think as much of the proceeds as possible, given the market conditions."
The share repurchase may give a boost to CIGNA's earnings in 1998, he said.
But CIGNA does not expect any "meaningful impact" to earnings from any charges associated with the sale of the business, Monroe said.

Monroe described the life business sale, valued at $1.6 billion, and the Healthsource acquisition for $1.7 billion as something of a swap for CIGNA as it increases its focus on the employee benefits and healthcare business.
CIGNA's life business was attractive, with returns of about 15 percent or so, Monroe said. But the company was a relatively small player in the field.
With Healthsource, Monroe said, CIGNA gains a better returns and growth prospects.
